baseline.name: Explicit naive substring search for each pattern
baseline.approach: For every pattern, try each possible starting position and compare characters.

archived.name: One libc strstr call per pattern
archived.time: Sum of substring-search costs over all P patterns; a naive search bound is O(P*W*Lmax), where W is word length and Lmax maximum pattern length. Actual strstr implementation cost is platform-dependent.
archived.space: O(1) explicit counter state; any library search workspace is implementation-dependent

why: Using the library expresses the same substring predicate clearly, but its implementation is a separate platform detail.
quantitative_comparison: The archive makes P strstr calls instead of P explicit search procedures. That alone says nothing about the number of character comparisons; a libc may optimize searches, but no version-specific work count or benchmark was established. No quantitative advantage is claimed.
tradeoffs: Library reuse reduces custom matching code. It assumes valid NUL-terminated strings, and actual time/workspace are libc-dependent.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
